repositories.name: metadata-service
repositories.reason: Owns the metadata store: must add per-column classification to the model and store, suggest it from source tags on schema discovery, expose a steward override endpoint, return it from the columns API and include it in metadata.dataset.changed.v1 events.

repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for event JSON Schemas and OpenAPI specs, so every changed event and endpoint (schema.discovered, dataset.changed, metadata-service, entitlements and consumption-gateway OpenAPI) must be updated here and released first.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: Shared typed clients for metadata-service-api (MetadataClient) and entitlements-api must expose the new column classification fields, the override call and the masked-columns field of access decisions.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Produces ingestion.schema.discovered.v1, whose column entries today carry only name/type/nullable, so the source column comment/tags (e.g. 'tags: pii,email') must be added for classification to be suggested.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Answers access decisions and must return the columns to mask when the requester lacks a pii:read grant, using classifications it gets from metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and metadata-service-api.

repositories.name: consumption-gateway
repositories.reason: Serves query results to data consumers and must mask the columns named in the entitlements access decision before returning results.

repositories.name: transformation-service
repositories.reason: Runs transformation rules and must read column classifications from metadata-service-api and apply PII-format validation rules to columns classified PII.

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: Cross-service end-to-end suite already covers ingestion, metadata-service, entitlements, consumption-gateway and transformation-service, and needs new scenarios for tag-to-classification, override, masking and PII transformation rules.

repositories.name: lineage-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1, which gains optional column fields, so its consumer must be re-tested against the new schema and sample events.

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and depends directly on platform-contracts (not the SDK), so it must be re-tested for tolerance of the new optional fields after a contracts upgrade.

repositories.name: notification-service
repositories.reason: Calls metadata-service-api through platform-sdk, so it must be re-tested after the SDK upgrade even though it does not use classification.

repositories.name: platform-catalog
repositories.reason: The plan adds no new topics, APIs or dependency edges, so catalog entities only need checking (and updating in the same PR if any team adds an integration).

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Only consumes consumption.access.logged.v1, which this plan does not change, and has no dependency on metadata-service, entitlements or the SDK.

considered_not_impacted.name: reporting-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Listed as a dataset.changed consumer in the metadata-service README, but the catalog marks it decommissioned with an archived repository, and topics.yaml does not list it as a consumer.

dependencies.contract: entitlements-api access decision endpoint (POST /v1/access/decisions, path inferred)
entitlements-api access decision endpoint (POST /v1/access/decisions, path inferred)

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional per-column 'comment' (raw source comment) and 'tags' (array of lower-case strings parsed from 'tags: a,b' in the comment or native source tags) to each entry of 'columns'.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional per-column 'classification' (PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII or null), 'classification_source' (SUGGESTED|STEWARD) and 'pii_type' (e.g. email, phone) to dataset.columns; classification changes are published with the existing change_type COLUMNS_CHANGED so the change_type enum is not widened.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Each column object gains optional 'classification', 'classification_source', 'suggested_classification', 'pii_type', 'classified_by' and 'classified_at' fields.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: New steward endpoint taking {classification, pii_type?, reason?} that sets or overrides a column's classification (source STEWARD), returns the updated column, and publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1; 400 on invalid value, 404 on unknown dataset or column.

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decisions (entitlements-api; exact path inferred)
contracts.description: Access-decision response gains 'masked_columns' (list of column names, empty when the requester holds pii:read or no column is PII) and optionally 'masking_reason'; existing allow/deny fields are unchanged.

contracts.name: POST /v1/queries (query-api; exact path inferred)
contracts.description: Response gains 'masked_columns' metadata, and values in those columns are replaced by a type-safe mask (null or a fixed mask string) for requesters without pii:read; column names, order and types are unchanged.

open_questions: What is the exact access-decision endpoint and request shape in platform-contracts/openapi/entitlements-service.yaml, and does it already receive the list of requested columns? (Not visible in this workspace; path above is inferred.)

What is the exact query-api results endpoint in platform-contracts/openapi/consumption-gateway.yaml, and what mask representation do consumers accept (null, fixed string such as '***', or format-preserving)?
Does a 'pii:read' grant type already exist in entitlements-service, or must it be created and assigned to current PII users before masking is enforced?
Does ingestion-service already capture source column comments/tags from connectors, or does each connector need work to read them?

Should a SUGGESTED PII classification (not yet confirmed by a steward) trigger masking and PII transformation rules, or only a STEWARD-confirmed one? Plan assumes the effective classification (steward override, else suggestion) is used.

What classification should existing and untagged columns get: null/unclassified (treated as non-PII, non-breaking) or a default such as INTERNAL? Is a backfill (re-discovery or bulk steward import) required before enforcement?
Who is allowed to call the steward override endpoint, and how does metadata-service authorize it today (it has no entitlements dependency in the catalog)?
Which tag-to-classification mapping is authoritative (e.g. pii/email/phone/ssn -> PII, confidential -> CONFIDENTIAL) and who owns it?
Which PII-format rules should transformation-service apply per pii_type (email, phone, national id, etc.), and should failures change transformation.result.published.v1 (currently assumed unchanged)?

Do metadata.dataset.changed.v1 consumers (search-indexer, lineage-service, entitlements-service) validate with additionalProperties:false? If so they must upgrade platform-contracts before metadata-service starts emitting the new fields.
Should consumption-gateway record masked columns in consumption.access.logged.v1 for audit? Assumed out of scope so usage-metering is not affected.

The metadata-service README lists reporting-service (decommissioned) as a consumer and omits lineage-service and search-indexer; the catalog also omits metadata-service's direct platform-contracts dependency seen in requirements.txt. Should these be corrected as part of this work?
